sources.title: Fresh isolated source-first monthly-income SQL review

claims.text: The preserved source requires per-user/per-month SUM(income) over income_records and filtering monthly totals strictly greater than 1000 while including user_id and month.
GROUP BY user_id, month plus HAVING SUM(income) > 1000 matches the source result grain and post-aggregation threshold.
Independent execution verifies multi-row aggregation, month/user separation, exact-1000 exclusion, 1001 inclusion, and preservation of separate equal-valued income rows.

validation.command: extract exact SQL candidate and execute independent SQLite adversarial fixture
validation.reported_stdout: PASS exact_candidate groups=6 strict_boundary=1 preaggregation_filter_trap=1 duplicate_value_rows=preserved
checks: exact candidate SQL parses and executes
groups by both user_id and month
aggregates before applying the monthly >1000 filter
equal-valued source rows are both counted
different users/months with equal totals remain distinct groups

boundary_tests.case: two sub-threshold rows 400+700 for one user/month
boundary_tests.expected: aggregate 1100 is retained; filtering occurs after aggregation

findings: The preserved source explicitly defines income_records(user_id, income, month), per-user/per-month summation, and a strict monthly-total >1000 filter.
The answer directly uses GROUP BY user_id, month and HAVING SUM(income) > 1000, matching the source grain and post-aggregation predicate.
The exact candidate SQL passes an independent adversarial SQLite fixture that distinguishes HAVING from erroneous pre-aggregation WHERE filtering.
The strict >1000 boundary is handled correctly: exactly 1000 is excluded while 1001 is retained.
Equal-valued income rows remain separate records and are both counted; the answer correctly warns against SUM(DISTINCT income) without a business uniqueness rule.
The candidate does not invent ordering, NULL, precision, schema, index, or production-performance facts and does not fabricate project experience.
